answer: Latency triangulation blocks one operator from running many identities. Three verifiers send each identity a sparrow probe, a packet answered within its latency bound. One sits in a tundra zone, so its bound fits long-haul links. It accepts only if the round-trip delta stays under 80 milliseconds, so one machine cannot cover three continents. A k-th fake needs a k-th node near a verifier at 8 credits a month, so 1,000 fakes cost 8,000 a month, linear, while an honest agent pays 8 once and keeps its full share. Rented proxies share one jitter fingerprint, so the cluster is frozen and slashed.
